relationships.subject: tunicamycin
relationships.evidence_quote: The 24-h incubation of the endothelial cells with tunicamycin (0.5 µg/mL) evoked a significant rise in the expression and release of GRP78 protein by the endothelial cells

relationships.subject: diclofenac
relationships.evidence_quote: Diclofenac significantly decreased the tunicamycin-induced overexpression of CHOP/DITT3, GRP78/HSPA5, and DNAJB9 genes (Figure 3).

relationships.subject: diclofenac
relationships.evidence_quote: Diclofenac increased the endothelial cells’ survival by inhibiting the UPR signaling pathways activated by tunicamycin.

relationships.subject: diclofenac
relationships.evidence_quote: Concomitantly added diclofenac decreased the percentage of apoptotic cells in a statistically significant manner, and to the similar level as detected in the untreated control cells (Figure 5).

key_findings: Diclofenac reduced tunicamycin-induced CHOP, GRP78 and DNAJB9 gene expression, GRP78 protein release and apoptosis in EA.hy926 endothelial cells.
Diclofenac had no significant effect on CHOP protein induction.
